new_statements.rule_in_words: For Gondi as sketched by Steever (data = Muria Gondi after Andres 1977): stress is not contrastive and falls on the word-initial syllable. No description of Aheri Gondi itself was opened; the nearest first-hand phonology actually read (Mathew & Mathew 2013, Far Western Muria of Gadchiroli, the sister lect of Aheri Gondi in Glottolog's 'Eastern Gondi') independently states non-contrastive, generally word-initial primary stress (sec. 2.4 pp. 6-7; sec. 9 p. 67), as do Tyler 1969 for Koya and the pan-Dravidian handbooks (Zvelebil 1970, Sjoberg 1971).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Steever's Gondi chapter snippet says nothing about secondary stress. (Mathew & Mathew 2013 for Far Western Muria: none described; Tyler 1969 Koya: weaker stress on non-initial long syllables.)
new_statements.exceptions: None in the Steever sentence. (Far Western Muria, Mathew & Mathew 2013 sec. 9: in some sentence frames and in disyllables with a short first vowel and a tap/flap onset to syllable 2, primary stress is word-final and the first syllable loses syllabicity, e.g. /taras/ [tə̯ˈɾas] 'snake', /uṛm/ [u̯ˈɽum] 'louse'.)
new_statements.domain_note: Steever: 'initial syllable of a word' -- word domain, citation forms; but the statement is a family-handbook generalisation over 'Gondi' whose data are Muria Gondi (west2408/muri1262), not Aheri Gondi (aher1237). Treat as second-hand for this key.
new_statements.identity_note: No source describing Aheri Gondi (aher1237 = Aheri/Etapalli/Sironcha/Bhamragarh Gondi of Gadchiroli, ISO esg, split in 2016 from 'Southern Gondi' [ggo]) was opened. The quoted sentence (Steever 1998:274) is a Gondi-wide handbook statement whose data are Muria Gondi (Andres 1977; Glottolog west2408/muri1262). The only full first-hand phonology read, Mathew & Mathew 2013, describes Far Western Muria (fmu, farw1235, Kurkheda tehsil, Gadchiroli) -- the sister of Aheri Gondi inside Glottolog's 'Eastern Gondi' (east2880) but a separate ISO language. Vaz 2005 and Veena 1965 describe Hill Madia of Bhamragad/Etapalli, which Glottolog files under Maria (mari1414), not under aher1237, although spoken in the same tehsils. Beine 1994's 'Southern dialect' = the old [ggo] (Aheri + Adilabad).

readall_conflicts: Neither newly opened work gives a word-stress position for Aheri Gondi itself. Srinivas 2016 states that Adilabad Gondi (a sister language, utno1237) "does not have overt stress" while positing an initial head foot; Nareti 2018 (Gondia-district Gondi) treats stress only as sentence-level emphasis with no word-level placement. Both are compatible with the "non-phonemic" half of the existing Steever 1998 statement (which is itself based on Muria Gondi) but Srinivas's "no overt stress" is a different type from "stress falls on the initial syllable"; the only Eastern-Gondi source with a placement statement remains Mathew & Mathew 2013 (Far Western Muria, read in the earlier reading: non-contrastive, generally first syllable). So: no direct contradiction for aher1237, but the initial-stress reading rests on Muria/Far Western Muria evidence, and the closest phonological study of a sister variety says there is no overt stress.
